LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar matters 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
•	 To understand obligation, lack of obligation and advice.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Actions Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Moods A5 flash cards 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: Character and Fun Activities 
cards (P.1.2) and Fun Activity/Chores memory cards 
(P.1.1)  
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Number cards (P.E.M.3)
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game Reference Sheet
•	 Big Book 
•	 Storytelling Pet Care tasks (A3) and Pet playing cards 
(P.S1)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 5: Days of the Week and 
Chores playing cards (P.1.5)
•	 Dice and Counters (1 per child) 
BEFORE CLASS
Check the teacher’s dashboard to see if the Ss have completed 
Mission 1.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (12’)
•	 Hello + register + booklets 
•	 Moods version 3
•	 Birthdays
•	 My Pet
2.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES (15’)
Today the students can tell the whole story choosing new 
variables. You can also encourage them to get up and act out

the story, pretending to be the different characters and moving 
around the classroom as if it were a stage.
NOTE: if your group still struggles with telling the story or 
you are short on time, have them tell it without any changes.
3.– ACTIVITY 3: GUESSING GAME (7’) 
P.1.1
P.1.2
P.1.2
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
Place a character card (P.1.2) on the table and shuffle the 
Fun Activity cards (P.1.2). One at a time, place the Fun Activity 
cards next to the character and ask the Ss: “What is Grandpa/
Pam/etc. doing?”. Encourage them to respond by saying “He/
she’s listening to music.”
> Main Activity
Place one of each of the Fun Activity cards (P.1.1 - without 
the chores) face up on the table so the Ss can use them as a 
visual reference. Then put the Character cards (P.1.2) next to 
the Fun Activity cards from Act. 2 (P.1.2) on the table face down.
Model the activity for the Ss. First, take a Character card (P.1.2) 
and place it face up on the table. Then take a Fun Activity card 
(P.1.2) but don’t show it to the Ss. They must guess what the 
character is doing by asking you questions.
So, for example, if you take a Mum card, they should ask, 
“What is Mum doing?” and then gesture to the Fun Activity 
cards (P.1.1) that are face up on the table. The Ss must use 
these cards as a reference to make a guess. The Ss must take 
it in turns to ask, “Is she watching TV?” to which you should 
answer, “No, she isn’t.” or “Yes, she’s watching TV.”
When a S guesses correctly, it’s their turn to take a Character 
card and a new Fun Activity card and repeat the steps above. 
Make sure every S participates at least once.

> Follow-Up
Take a Character card and a Fun Activity card. Ask wrong 
questions on purpose by saying actions that aren’t depicted 
on your card, for example, “Is Dad playing in the park?” to 
which Ss should answer, “No, he isn’t playing in the park. He 
is watching TV.”
4.– ACTIVITY 6: NUMBERS (VERSION 3) (5’) 
P.E.M.3
55
> Warm-Up
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
If you feel like your group needs it, quickly review the numbers 
by using the Number cards (P.E.M.3.) without the jokers. Turn 
over one card at a time and, as a group, say, “It’s number 55!” 
> Main Activity
This is a relay game. Divide the class into two teams. Get 
each team to form a line in front of the whiteboard. Give each 
team a whiteboard marker, draw a card from the deck (P.E.M.3.) 
and call out the number. One S from each team must run to 
the board and write the number. Keep saying numbers until 
every S has written one. Then check these numbers using the 
cards. The team with the most correct numbers written on 
the board wins. 
NOTE: it might be helpful to divide the board into two (Team 1, 
Team 2) and to make each team line up in front of their section. 
5.– ACTIVITY 9: PREPOSITIONS (4’)
> Warm-Up
The Ss should perform the following actions to rehearse 
the movements.
•	 March in line. (all the Ss march in a single file line)
•	 Hide under the table.

•	 Walk next to a friend.
•	 Stand between two chairs.
•	 Jump behind the teacher. (all the Ss jump on the spot 
behind the teacher)
•	 Run in front of the (white) board. (all the Ss run on 
the spot in front of the board)
•	 Sit on a chair.
> Main Activity
Then play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance 
to it.
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.) 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.

6.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
7.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.

BONUS
ACTIVITY 5: DAYS OF THE WEEK CARD GAME
Story Comprehension
Monday
Tuesday
Saturday
Sunday
Wednesday
Thursday
Friday
4
P.1.5
Monday
> How to Play
This is based on the traditional card game Go Fish. The point 
of the game is to find pairs of matching cards by asking the 
other players for them. In this case, Ss must match the day of 
the week and the chore that Pam and Paul had to do that day. 
> Warm-Up
Bring a SB with you and use p.4 (Story Comprehension) as a 
visual aid. Preferably, the worksheet would have been completed 
previously. 
Show the Monday card (P.1.5) and ask the Ss “What must 
Pam and Paul do on Monday?”. Ss must answer, “On Monday, 
Pam and Paul must wash Billy.”. Review the whole week in 
the same manner:
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Monday?” 	
 
“On Monday, Pam and Paul must wash Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Tuesday?” 	
 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Wednesday?”  
“On Wednesday, Pam and Paul must take Billy for 
a walk.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Thursday?” 	  
“On Thursday, Pam and Paul must pick up Billy’s poo.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Friday?” 	
 
“On Friday, Pam and Paul must give Billy some water.” 
•	 “What must Pam and Paul do on Saturday?” 	  
“On Saturday, Pam and Paul must brush Billy.” 
•	 “What happens on Sunday?” 	
 
“On Sunday, Billy is with Grandma.” 
> Main Activity
To play, you should first shuffle the cards (P.1.5) while saying, 
“Mix, mix, mix” and have the Ss say, “Stop!”

Then deal three cards to each S and put the rest of the cards 
in a pile face down on the table. Explain to the Ss that they 
must find pairs. Ss must ask another S for a card and try to 
match it with one of the cards in their hand. They can either 
ask for the day of the week or the chore: 
•	 “Jane, have you got Friday?”
•	 “Jane, have you got ‘brush Billy’?”
Jane should either:
•	 Say “Yes, I have, here you are!” and hand it over to 
the S who asked for it. 
•	 Say “No, I haven’t. Take a card!” and the S who asked 
must pick up a card from the deck. 
When a S finds a pair, they must then place the pair face 
up on the table and say, “I’ve got a pair!”. After that, it is the 
next Ss’ turn. 
The game continues with the Ss taking turns asking for the 
card they need from the other players. If a player gets all their 
cards stolen, they have to draw a card from the pile on their turn. 
The game is over when there are no cards left on the deck in 
the middle, or when time is up. At this point, ask the Ss one by 
one, “How many pairs have you got?” and the S must answer, 
“I’ve got five pairs.” The S with the most pairs is the winner.
NOTE: if you have a small group, you might want to halve 
the deck to speed up the activity. 
> Follow-Up
Take the winner’s pairs and ask the group: “What pairs has 
Jane got?”. Point to the cards and elicit from the whole group: 
“On Tuesday, Pam and Paul must feed Billy. On Monday...”
